data.title: Vietnamese partners of Trump Organization plan Trump Tower in Hanoi, sources say
data.description:
By Francesco Guarascio and Khanh Vu

Vietnamese business partners of the Trump Organization are planning a skyscraper in Hanoi, three people with knowledge of the new project said.

It is one of three Trump-branded projects in the works in the Southeast Asian nation. A $1.5 billion Trump-branded golf complex is being developed near Hanoi by local partners of the Trump Organization. A separate Trump Tower is planned in Ho Chi Minh City, people involved with the project have said.

All the projects are being developed at no cost to the Trump Organization, which earns money from the use of its brand, operating fees and property sales, one person with direct knowledge of the plans said.

Vietnamese government officials met the Trump Organization's partners, which include Kinh Bac City Development Holding , on Thursday to discuss the Hanoi project, according to two of the sources.

The meeting took place shortly after Washington announced possible new tariffs of up to 35% on Vietnam, which could be cut to 20% if a trade deal is struck, they said.

One of the people said the project was first submitted to the government in May and that it had not yet received approval.

All sources declined to be named as the information was not public. The plans for a new Trump Tower in Hanoi are being reported here for the first time.

The Trump Organization, US President Donald Trump's family business, was not immediately available for comment outside US working hours. Vietnam's government and Kinh Bac City Development did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

data.title: Norse Atlantic Receives Termination Notices For Aircraft Leases
data.description:
By Dominic Chopping

Norse Atlantic said that it has received lease termination notices from the lessors of its entire fleet of aircraft.

The Norwegian long-haul low-cost airline suspended all of its flights Thursday after warning that it will file for bankruptcy if financing can't be urgently secured.

The carrier operates a fleet of 12 Boeing 787 Dreamliners, and it said in a statement Friday that the lessors of the aircraft have now issued lease termination notices for all 12 aircraft.

"The company contests the validity of the termination notices," Norse said.

The airline has been exploring a potential sale, merger or partnership for several months after being hit by soaring fuel costs following the start of the Iran war. The high fuel prices, airspace restrictions and longer routes resulting from Middle East conflicts also saw a leasing agreement with India's IndiGo recently end.

Norse has been in talks to secure financing to meet its short-term liquidity needs, and it said in recent days that it is in talks with investors over a possible takeover that would include a financing solution.

Talks to secure short-term financing continue, but Norse said Friday that there can be no assurance that a viable solution will be found.

Write to Dominic Chopping at dominic.chopping@wsj.com

data.title: China stocks surge most in two years as Beijing vows stronger market support
data.description:
China's share benchmarks jumped 4% and the yuan rose on Friday, after Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council meeting that called for a bigger role by "national team" investors to stabilise a falling stock market.

Chinese stocks have struggled this year despite policy easing, reflecting investor concerns over weak domestic demand, a prolonged property downturn and uncertainty over the economic outlook hurt by trade wars and geopolitics.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index ended 4.2% up and the blue-chip CSI300 index was 3.7% higher at the close, both notching their biggest daily gains since October 2024 when China rolled out massive stimulus measures to revive the market.

China's tech-focused STAR 50 Index surged 15%, the biggest one-day jump in two years.

The rally also spread to Hong Kong, where the Hang Seng Index gained 1.9% while the Hang Seng Tech Index <.HSTECH> jumped 6%.

In Beijing's strongest gesture yet to support a stock market that had fallen to 16-month lows, the cabinet said "capital markets were crucial to the broader economy," state media Xinhua reported. The cabinet added that Central Huijin - the domestic unit of sovereign wealth fund China Investment Corp - would enhance its role as a quasi-stabilisation fund to ensure ample liquidity.

The meeting also called for better policies to encourage long-term funds to invest in the stock market, and for measures to strengthen defences against risks spilling over from overseas markets.

"It's a shot in the arm for markets," said Kenny Ng, a strategist at Everbright Securities International in Hong Kong.

"Sentiment has been downbeat for so long. There hasn't been much good news to trade on. At least now there's something to count on: the national team will come to the rescue if things really turn south."

The Chinese yuan gained 0.1% against the dollar in offshore trading, reversing earlier weakness to hit its strongest in three weeks. The currency is nearing its firmest level in four years.

"It's very rare that Executive meeting of the State Council would make such direct comments. Last time it happened was 2024 when they rolled out a liquidity support package," said Jason Chan, a Hong Kong-based strategest at Bank of East Asia.

Given the current low investor expectations, any incremental supportive policies would help boost confidence, said Meng Lei, China equity strategist at UBS Securities.

The latest statement follows the margin lending relaxation and trading fee reductions announced over the weekend, underscoring the government's growing determination to stabilise markets.

LSEG data showed trading volume surged across broad-based benchmarks and sub-indices after the midday break, pointing to a sharp improvement in investor sentiment.

The CSI Semiconductor Industry Index (.CSI931865) and the STAR Chip Index (.STARCHIP) both shot up more than 17%.

Indices tracking China's AI , cloud computing (.CSI930851) and consumer electronics stocks (.CSI931494) jumped more than 10%.

But some analysts said it was too early to suggest the market was near a bottom as support from the national team alone was unlikely to lead to a sustained rally.

"There is an increasingly clear signal that Chinese authorities are uncomfortable with the extent of the equity market selloff," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank.

"I would distinguish between a turning point in policy resolve and a turning point in market fundamentals... A policy-induced bounce needs to evolve into a fundamentally driven recovery before we can confidently call it a durable bottom."

Also on Friday, Xinhua Finance reported that regulators will launch a campaign to further tighten rules on share sales by controlling shareholders of listed companies. Regulators will also guard against listings by "pseudo-tech" companies, or firms that inflate earnings, the state media said.

data.title: Ortelius moves to half-yearly reporting with immediate effect and will not publish a report for the third quarter of 2026
data.description:
The Board of Directors of Ortelius International AB (publ) ("Ortelius" or the "Company") has resolved that the Company will move from quarterly to half-yearly financial reporting with immediate effect. The Company will therefore not publish an interim report for the period January–September 2026. The next financial report will be the year-end report for 2026. The Company's financial calendar has been updated.

This is an unofficial translation of the Swedish press release. In the event of any discrepancy between the Swedish original and this English translation, the Swedish version shall prevail.

Under the Nasdaq First North Growth Market Rulebook, companies whose shares are traded on First North must report on a half-yearly basis through a half-year report and a year-end report. Quarterly reporting is voluntary. Ortelius has until now reported quarterly.

The decision is based on the Company's financial position. The quarterly reports are voluntary and are prepared with the help of external providers. The Company currently does not have the financial means to bear the cost of reporting that is not mandatory. With this change, the Company reports in accordance with the basic requirements of the rulebook.

"In Ortelius's current situation, every krona must be prioritised. It cannot be justified to spend money on reports that are not mandatory. Half-yearly reporting is what the rules require, and we will continue to keep the market informed of everything material on an ongoing basis," says Herman Weberg, acting CEO and CFO of Ortelius.

data.title: French Inflation Slides on Drop in Fuel Prices — Update
data.description:
By Ed Frankl

Inflation in France fell more than expected in November as fuel prices declined, but remained too high for the European Central Bank, which next month is expected to raise its key interest rate for a third time since the start of the war between the U.S. and Iran.

Consumer prices in the eurozone's second-largest economy were 3.2% higher than in the same month of 2025, a lower annual rate of inflation than the 3.7% recorded in October, France's statistics office said Friday. Economists polled last week by The Wall Street Journal expected a 3.6% rate of inflation.

Inflation in France climbed to its highest level in nearly three years in October, from an annual rate of just 1.1% in February, before the first U.S. airstrikes on Iran.

Oil prices have fallen since the outcome of U.S. midterm elections fueled hopes of a lasting resolution to the conflict, although they remain above prewar levels. As a result, prices of gasoline and other fuels have declined.

However, European natural gas prices remain near multiyear highs, which will keep household energy prices elevated throughout the colder winter months.

The ECB has raised its key rate twice so far this year, judging that the surge in energy prices was too great to ignore. Investors are primed for another hike before the end of the year.

The EU said last week that it expects French inflation to peak at 4.3% in the first quarter of 2027 due to further increases in energy prices and how they pass through into food and services.

Yet incoming data shows few signs of those energy costs spilling over into other parts of the economy. Services inflation, for instance, fell in November due to a sharp decrease in prices for accommodation and transport services.

It comes as France's economy appears to have been hit harder by the war than its neighbors. Gross domestic product sank 0.2% in the third quarter, dented by a drop in exports and lower private investment.

Investors have grown more concerned in recent months over the country's public finances, which sent government bond yields rising. Those higher bond yields, while ratcheting up nervousness around the economy, could help the ECB as they tighten monetary conditions before the central bank needs to raise rates.

French consumer spending was flat on month in October, data also published Friday showed, coming in the month when consumer confidence hit its lowest level in more than three years. While surveys of purchasing managers showed steady economic growth in Germany, there was a deepening downturn in activity in France.

Write to Ed Frankl at edward.frankl@wsj.com

data.title: Gods Unchained to Introduce Card Essence on December 1st
data.description:
Gods Unchained will introduce Card Essence with Conquest Season 6 on December 1st. Players finishing in the top 10 on the leaderboard will earn the resource to replace missing duplicate cards in Epic and Legendary Shine upgrades.

Refer to the official tweet by GODS:

Gods Unchained
@GodsUnchained

The missing piece has a name: Card Essence. âœ¨

Starting with Conquest Season 6 on December 1, top 10 leaderboard finishers will earn Card Essence to replace missing duplicates in Epic and Legendary Shine upgrades.

Climb. Claim. Shine.

👉 https://t.co/AUC89iZJYN pic.twitter.com/3NvbCs5yyt

Nov 26, 2026

GODS Info

Gods Unchained is a revolutionary addition to the gaming landscape, operating within the blockchain and cryptocurrency domain. As a free-to-play online trading card game, it draws parallels with popular games like Magic: The Gathering Arena. However, it differentiates itself by offering a unique economic model where players can earn real-world value, thereby subverting the traditional gaming commerce paradigm where in-game purchases lack resale value.

The gameplay and strategy in Gods Unchained mirror that of conventional online card games. However, the distinction lies in its economic infrastructure. Instead of merely simulating in-game currencies like “gold” or “credits”, Gods Unchained employs a tangible currency with inherent monetary value. This real-world financial implication augments the gaming experience as players can trade cards in the game’s marketplace. Winning matches yields more cards, adding an extra layer of competitiveness and incentive. The game is also expanding its user base by employing effective promotional strategies such as tournaments and is in the process of launching a mobile version to enhance its global reach.

The GODS token stands central to the Gods Unchained ecosystem. Classified as an ERC-20 token, it serves multiple purposes: from facilitating in-game transactions in the marketplace to the creation of NFTs and acquiring rewards. The token has a capped supply of 500 million units, distributed among various stakeholders, including players and developers. Furthermore, players can securely store their GODS tokens and associated NFT cards in web 3.0 wallets, such as MetaMask. Notably, beyond its transactional value, the GODS token also empowers players with a governance role. They can exercise voting rights on game-related decisions, epitomizing the game’s community-centric ethos.

data.title: REG - UzNIF JSC - Publication of unaudited results for nine months
data.description:
RNS Number : 9858E National Investment Fund Uzbekistan 27 November 2026  

The “National Investment Fund of the Republic of Uzbekistan” JSC

LEI: 254900QS7VSE8KIDBL52

Publication of unaudited results for the nine months ended 30 September 2026

London and Tashkent, 27 November 2026 – The “National Investment Fund of the Republic of Uzbekistan” JSC (“UzNIF” or the “Company”) (LSE: UZNF, UZ20; RSE “Toshkent”: UZNF) today announces its unaudited results for the nine months ended 30 September 2026.

The Q3 2026 Report will shortly become available on the Company’s website at https://www.uznif.com/en-uz/corporate-governance#information-disclosures.

The condensed interim financial statements included in the Q3 2026 Report are unaudited and have not been reviewed by the Fund’s independent auditor.

Highlights:

  • NAV per share was UZS 6.2421 as at 30 September 2026. On a like-for-like basis, after adjusting the 31 December 2025 figure for the five-for-one share consolidation completed in April 2026, NAV per share increased by approximately 5.7%, from UZS 5.9082. The increase was driven principally by portfolio valuation movements during the period.
  • Total NAV increased by approximately 5.7% in UZS terms to UZS 31,549 billion (USD 2.67 billion) as at 30 September 2026, compared with UZS 29,862 billion (USD 2.48 billion) as at 31 December 2025.
  • Profit for the nine-month period was UZS 1,936.6 billion, driven primarily by net unrealised gains on equity investments of UZS 2,174.8 billion, alongside gross dividend income of UZS 356.3 billion.
  • As at 30 September 2026, the ordinary share price was UZS 6.61, 42.15% above the UZS 4.65 IPO offer price, while the GDR price was USD 34.40, 37.60% above the USD 25.00 IPO offer price.
  • The Fund recognised gross dividend income of UZS 356.3 billion from 4 portfolio companies during the nine-month period, with UZS 223.7 billion received by 30 September 2026. However, several portfolio companies have not yet approved their dividends for FY 2025.
  • The Fund's portfolio valuations remained unchanged from H1 2026. The year-end valuation process is underway, using the latest available portfolio companies’ financial information to determine fair values as at 31 December 2026. The updated valuations will be incorporated into the Fund's monthly NAV calculation and 2026 Annual Report.
  • The Fund continued to make progress on portfolio company governance and transformation. As at 30 September 2026, members of the Trustee’s investment team served on the supervisory boards of all portfolio companies, 10 new independent supervisory board members had been elected, and three CFOs had been appointed. Transformation programmes had been finalised for six portfolio companies, with a further five under review and two in development.

Events after the reporting period:

Uzbekhydroenergo’s Supervisory Board recommended a dividend of UZS 21.26 per share for the 2025 financial year. If approved by shareholders, this would result in approximately UZS 66 billion in dividends attributable to the Fund.

On 6 November 2026, Uzbekhydroenergo registered an additional share issue of approximately UZS 2.97 trillion, to be funded through the capitalisation of retained earnings and previously contributed funds. The new shares are to be allocated 60% to the Ministry of Economy and Finance and 40% to UzNIF, without additional cash contributions. As at the date of the report, the placement and allocation of the new shares to UzNIF has not yet been finalised.

Marius Dan, General Director of FE “Franklin Templeton Asset Management” LLC, trustee of the Company, commented:

“We are pleased with the progress made during the first nine months of 2026. NAV per share increased by approximately 5.7% over the period, supported by the portfolio valuation update earlier in the year. We also continued to strengthen governance across the portfolio and work with our companies to improve their operations and create long-term value.

In October, we welcomed investors and research analysts to Tashkent for our 2nd Investor Day. The event provided an opportunity to engage directly with portfolio company management teams and gain a deeper understanding of Uzbekistan’s reform agenda and the outlook across our portfolio. About UzNIF

The "National Investment Fund of the Republic of Uzbekistan" JSC ("UzNIF") was established pursuant to Presidential Decree RP-303 dated 27 August 2024 as part of Uzbekistan's economic reform programme, with a mandate to support the development of the country's capital markets, attract international investment and enhance the value of state-owned enterprises. UzNIF's investment objective is to maximise shareholder returns and net asset value per share through active ownership, improved governance and disciplined capital allocation. Its diversified portfolio comprises equity stakes ranging from 25% to 40% in 13 state-owned enterprises across sectors including transport, financial services, energy, utilities and telecommunications.

UzNIF is listed on the London Stock Exchange and the Republican Stock Exchange "Toshkent". FE "Franklin Templeton Asset Management" LLC, a Tashkent-based wholly owned indirect subsidiary of Franklin Templeton, Inc., acts as trustee and fund manager of UzNIF.
